newsitem.title: UK: UK bank shares slide amid light profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: UK bank shares slide amid light profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in UK bank stocks fell in early trade on Thursday led by Barclays Plc as investors took profits after a long bull run in the sector over recent weeks, said dealers.
The June 2 listing of the Halifax Building Society has boosted the financial sector as institutional investors are expected to build stakes in the Halifax.

"The banks have been strong over the last few weeks and you have seen a real scramble for stock by underweight funds, after a squeeze like that its inevitable you will see some sort of a sell-off," said one dealer.
"People may also be concerned that with the Halifax auction so imminent they are pricing in too much of a scarcity premium into the sector," he added.
The bank sector also tends to correlate closely to the long end of the gilt market which has waned since a run up shortly after the May 1 election result.

Abbey National shares were off 18p at 909, Barclays were down 13 at 1244, Royal Bank of Scotland shed 11p to 622, Standard Chartered fell 6-1/2p to 994. Shares in the banking sector have gained some 25 percent since the year began.
